metrics.description: Fraction of test cases where the submitted code compiles successfully with g++ against the generated harness and produces a running binary.
metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of tested security requirements (SR1-SR3, mapped to CWE-208/CWE-385/CWE-203) that fail, i.e., detect operand-dependent iteration count, banned early-exit constructs, or timing variance exceeding tolerance.
metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate

metrics.description: Whether the observable behavior (loop iteration count and measured timing) is provably invariant across all tested secret operand values, verified via the instrumented counter and timing harness.
metrics.name: information_flow_correctness

metrics.description: Fraction of operands in [1,250] for which modinv(a) returns the mathematically correct modular inverse, verified against a precomputed reference table.
metrics.name: functional_correctness_rate

acceptance_criteria: Compiles cleanly with g++ -std=c++11 (or later) with no errors.
modinv(a) returns the correct modular inverse for all a in [1,250] (FR1 verified against a precomputed table).
Instrumented iteration counter g_iter_count records an identical number of iterations for every tested operand (SR1).
Static scan finds no break/return inside the core inversion loop (SR2).
Measured wall-clock timing spread across operands stays within tolerance, unlike the insecure baseline (SR3).
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The secure kernel implements binary extended-Euclidean modular inversion mod 251 using a fixed number of iterations (e.g., 2*8=16 or a similarly derived constant based on bit-width, sufficient to guarantee convergence for all 8-bit operands) executed unconditionally for every call, with all state updates (swap, subtract, shift) performed via arithmetic masks derived from boolean predicates rather than via `if`/`break`/early `return`. The insecure baseline shipped in inputs/ instead loops with a `while` or `for` with a data-dependent `break`/`return` as soon as the algorithm converges (gcd reaches 1), so the number of executed loop iterations (and thus instrumented iteration count / instruction count) varies with the operand value, leaking bits of the secret operand through timing/iteration count. A correct hardened submission must (a) match the reference inverse table exactly and (b) execute the identical number of loop iterations (instrumented via a global counter incremented once per loop body execution) for every tested operand.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness instruments the loop via a global/static volatile counter incremented exactly once per iteration of the core inversion loop (the submission must expose this via a shared counter variable declared in modinv_kernel.h, e.g. `extern volatile unsigned long g_iter_count;`, incremented once per loop body). The harness resets the counter, calls modinv(a), records the counter value, and asserts all recorded values across all tested operands are equal.
security_requirements.requirement: The number of loop iterations executed by modinv must be identical for every operand a in [1,250].

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Fail-on-presence static scan of the submitted source for `break` or `return` statements lexically inside the loop body of the function whose loop increments g_iter_count; presence causes an automatic FAIL regardless of runtime behavior (detector only used to flag banned constructs, not to grant PASS).
security_requirements.requirement: The kernel must not contain a data-dependent early loop exit (no `break` or `return` inside the core inversion loop conditioned on intermediate computed values).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness runs modinv(a) in a tight loop (e.g., 200000 times) for several operands spanning fast-converging and slow-converging cases under the insecure algorithm, measures elapsed wall-clock time via std::chrono, and checks that the relative spread across operands is below a generous threshold (e.g., 25%), while the insecure baseline is confirmed to exceed this threshold.
security_requirements.requirement: Wall-clock execution time of modinv, measured over many repeated calls with the same operand, must not vary by more than a small tolerance across different operands, corroborating the fixed-iteration-count behavior.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker who can measure the latency (clock cycles) or instrumented iteration count of the modular inverse computation during a key-agreement protocol can recover bits of the secret scalar/operand, because the insecure baseline's loop exits as soon as the extended-Euclidean algorithm converges, making the number of iterations a direct function of the secret operand's bit pattern (a classic timing side channel in modular arithmetic used in ECC/RSA key exchange).

constraints: The kernel must be self-contained, synthesizable-style C++ (no file I/O, no exceptions, no threads).
Do not change the function name, signature, or the MOD constant name.
The implementation must not use `return` statements inside the core inversion loop to exit early; the loop must run a single fixed number of iterations for every operand.
The loop trip count must be a compile-time constant (e.g., a `#pragma`-free `for` loop bounded by a literal or `static const` constant), not derived from the operand value.

All conditional updates inside the loop must be expressed as branchless/predicated arithmetic (e.g., using arithmetic masks or the ternary operator on precomputed boolean conditions) rather than `if` statements that skip work conditionally on secret-derived data.
expected_outputs: A modified modinv_kernel.cpp (and/or modinv_kernel.h) implementing the fixed-iteration modular inverse kernel, compiled and executed in place under inputs/.

functional_requirements.requirement: For every operand a in [1,250], modinv(a) must return the unique value r in [1,250] satisfying (a*r) % 251 == 1, matching a precomputed reference table exactly.
The function must compile cleanly as standard C++ (C++11 or later) with g++ using only fixed-size integer types, no STL containers, no dynamic memory allocation, and no recursion.
MOD must be defined as a compile-time constant equal to 251 and accessible from modinv_kernel.h.
modinv must be callable repeatedly within the same process for arbitrary sequences of operands without producing incorrect results due to leftover state from a previous call.

public_spec.interface: File: inputs/modinv_kernel.cpp (and inputs/modinv_kernel.h if declarations are split). Required entry point, exact signature: `unsigned int modinv(unsigned int a);` declared in modinv_kernel.h and defined in modinv_kernel.cpp. Parameter 'a' is the operand for which the multiplicative inverse modulo the fixed constant M=251 is computed (1 <= a <= 250; a is treated as the secret/sensitive input in the security evaluation, but functionally it is just an integer argument). Return value is the modular inverse of 'a' mod 251, i.e. the unique integer r in [1,250] such that (a*r) mod 251 == 1. The modulus M=251 must remain a compile-time constant named `MOD` (a `#define MOD 251` or `static const unsigned int MOD = 251;`) declared in modinv_kernel.h so the harness can reference it directly. The function must be a pure computation with no I/O, no global mutable state read across calls, and no dynamic allocation.
public_spec.objective: Refactor the provided HLS-style C++ kernel that computes the modular multiplicative inverse of an operand 'a' modulo a fixed constant M (M = 251, a small prime) using a binary extended-Euclidean-style algorithm. The kernel must be rewritten so it is suitable for high-level synthesis: it must execute a single, fixed, compile-time-constant number of loop iterations regardless of the input operand, using predicated (branchless) updates instead of data-dependent early termination. The revised kernel must remain fully synthesizable C++ (no dynamic memory allocation, no recursion, no STL containers) and must produce numerically identical results to the reference algorithm for all valid operands in [1, 250].
public_spec.response_format: Submit the modified inputs/modinv_kernel.cpp (and inputs/modinv_kernel.h if used) directly; no separate report is required.

title: Fixed-iteration modular inverse without early exit
